questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.topic: The emergency that undoes the right

stimulus.body: In danger, the right was suspended. The suspension was temporary. When danger passed, the right returned. Emergency was the trigger.

questions.stem: Item 0053 examines a source on emergency suspension of rights.

options.text: The source mainly ties suspension to emergency.
The source mainly defends individual liberty.
The source mainly records a compromise.
The source mainly argues for absolute monarchy.

questions.explanation: Suspension follows emergency, so the trigger is danger, not monarchy or liberty.

questions.topic: A right that can always be set aside
questions.stem: Item 0055 examines a right always set aside.

options.text: Power becomes legitimate only through the consent of those governed.
options.misconception: treats consent as the sole source of authority

options.text: Power is legitimate when it preserves inherited rank and tradition.
A defeasible right yields to the common good.
Power is legitimate when it serves the common good of all.

questions.explanation: A defeasible right yields to the common good, which is its defining feature.
